title_bn: From the Ganges to the Padma: The water dispute flows on
title_en: From the Ganges to the Padma: The water dispute flows on
summary_bn: With the 1996 treaty expiring in December, Bangladesh needs a new agreement guaranteeing fair dry-season flows and addressing upstream withdrawals and river management round the year
summary_en: With the 1996 treaty expiring in December, Bangladesh needs a new agreement guaranteeing fair dry-season flows and addressing upstream withdrawals and river management round the year
body_bn:
দ্য বিজনেস স্ট্যান্ডার্ড-এর প্রতিবেদন অনুযায়ী — From the Ganges to the Padma: The water dispute flows on। With the 1996 treaty expiring in December, Bangladesh needs a new agreement guaranteeing fair dry-season flows and addressing upstream withdrawals and river management round the year

Beyond the bargaining over water shares are people whose livelihoods depend on the flow. Photo: Syed Zakir Hossain "> Beyond the bargaining over water shares are people whose livelihoods depend on the flow. Photo: Syed Zakir Hossain In a popular story, Mughal emperor Akbar (1542–1605) challenges his witty courtier Birbal to count the waves of the Yamuna River as it flows past Agra, one of the capitals of the monarch. Birbal accepts the challenge, as he always does, but says he can give an accurate count only if a royal decree stipulates that no wave may merge with another and no new wave may arrive until he finishes counting. The emperor is amused by his courtier's quick wit.

Counting the Yamuna's waves may have been only Birbal's problem in the popular story, but agreeing on a new arrangement for sharing the Ganges is a challenge for Bangladesh and India. The task is not merely to divide the water that reaches Farakka, but to ensure that upstream activities do not leave Bangladesh with inadequate water.

The issue is urgent. The 30-year Ganges Water Sharing Treaty, signed on 12 December 1996, will expire in December 2026. It was the second agreement between Bangladesh and India on sharing the Ganges waters, following the 1977 treaty. Water Resources Minister Shahid Uddin Chowdhury Anee said on 8 October that Bangladesh wants a new, longer-term agreement with a guarantee clause to protect its dry-season water share. He expressed hope that an agreement could be reached before the deadline.

India's response has been guarded. On 9 October, India's foreign ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal reiterated that river-related issues between the two countries fall within the ambit of the Joint Rivers Commission (JRC). Earlier, he said technical-level meetings on the Ganges treaty were continuing. Bangladesh's Foreign Affairs State Minister Humayun Kobir has also stressed the need for dialogue and diplomacy, with international law taken into consideration.

The immediate priority is to avoid uncertainty after 12 December. The two countries could agree to extend the existing treaty as an interim measure while negotiating a new long-term agreement. After the 1977 treaty expired, the two countries signed several memorandums of understanding (MoUs) to bridge the gaps before reaching a new long-term agreement.

The apple of discord is the Farakka Barrage, a 2,240-metre-long structure in the Indian province of West Bengal, about 18 kilometres upstream of the Bangladesh border. Commissioned in 1975, the Farakka Barrage was designed to divert up to 40,000 cusecs or, cubic feet per second, of water through a feeder canal into the Bhagirathi-Hooghly river system to improve navigability and maintain Kolkata port.

One cusec is equivalent to about 28.32 litres of water flowing past a given place every second. The Kolkata port lies 232 kilometres upstream from the mouth of the Hooghly River, where it empties into the Bay of Bengal, and is accessible to ships through the river.

title_bn: Taliban bans cricket coverage on radio stations in Kandahar province
title_en: Taliban bans cricket coverage on radio stations in Kandahar province
summary_bn: Broadcasters say the authorities have prohibited match commentary, news reports and even coverage of results.
summary_en: Broadcasters say the authorities have prohibited match commentary, news reports and even coverage of results.
body_bn:
দ্য বিজনেস স্ট্যান্ডার্ড-এর প্রতিবেদন অনুযায়ী — Taliban bans cricket coverage on radio stations in Kandahar province। Broadcasters say the authorities have prohibited match commentary, news reports and even coverage of results.

The Taliban authorities have banned radio stations in Afghanistan's southern Kandahar province from broadcasting cricket-related content, including match commentary, news reports and results, according to local broadcasters and a provincial source.

The directive was issued by the provincial Information and Culture Department on Saturday (14 November), two broadcasters and a departmental source told AFP yesterday (15 November).

A source at the department, who requested anonymity because he was not authorised to speak to the media, confirmed that "cricket coverage is banned".

"Both commentary and news coverage, or even reporting about their winning result, is also banned," he told AFP, without providing further details.

The head of a local radio station said it had received a phone call from the Information and Culture Department informing it that cricket could no longer be covered on radio.

The manager of another Kandahar-based radio station also confirmed receiving the directive, saying the authorities had instructed that "anything related to cricket is banned for now".

Both broadcasters spoke to AFP on condition of anonymity for security reasons.

title_bn: 3 sued over gang rape, filming of ninth-grader in Netrokona
title_en: 3 sued over gang rape, filming of ninth-grader in Netrokona
summary_bn: The accused allegedly threatened to upload the video on Facebook if she disclosed the incident to anyone.
summary_en: The accused allegedly threatened to upload the video on Facebook if she disclosed the incident to anyone.
body_bn:
দ্য বিজনেস স্ট্যান্ডার্ড-এর প্রতিবেদন অনুযায়ী — 3 sued over gang rape, filming of ninth-grader in Netrokona। The accused allegedly threatened to upload the video on Facebook if she disclosed the incident to anyone.

A case has been filed over the alleged gang rape of a ninth-grade student in Kendua upazila of Netrokona.

The victim's father filed the case against three people with Kendua Police Station yesterday (15 November), said Md Tarikul Islam, officer-in-charge (OC) of the police station.

The accused, Md Shuvo, 24, Md Nure Alam, 33, and Shah Alam, 31, all residents of the upazila, have been absconding since the incident, police said.

According to the case statement, Shuvo had been in a relationship with the girl for nearly four years. On Friday night, while her father was away, he allegedly lured her out of the house with a promise of marriage and took her to a nearby crop field, saying they would wait there for an auto-rickshaw.

Later, Nure Alam and Shah Alam arrived at the spot at around 10:30pm. All three allegedly raped the girl in turn and recorded the incident, according to the complaint.

Terrified, the teenager first sought shelter at a classmate's house in a neighbouring village. However, after failing to find refuge there, she spent the night on the veranda of another classmate's house in a different village.

title_bn: Formula 1's one-race wonders
title_en: Formula 1's one-race wonders
summary_bn: Making it to Formula 1 is the undoubted pinnacle of any racing driver’s career – but what became of some of those who only had one shot?
summary_en: Making it to Formula 1 is the undoubted pinnacle of any racing driver’s career – but what became of some of those who only had one shot?
body_bn:
বিবিসি স্পোর্ট-এর প্রতিবেদন অনুযায়ী — Formula 1's one-race wonders। Making it to Formula 1 is the undoubted pinnacle of any racing driver’s career – but what became of some of those who only had one shot?

A chance to sit in the cockpit, on the grid, at motorsport's top table: Formula 1. The very pinnacle of everything you've strived for in your whole life.

"I sang the Grand Prix theme tune while I was sat on the grid. I thought I was watching it on telly," says Tiff Needell - one of 166 lucky or unlucky drivers, depending on your standing in motorsport, who graced an F1 race only once.

There are many reasons why a driver may only get one chance to race elite sport's fastest and most sophisticated machines, and, although F1's super subs were more of a feature in the 1960s and 1970s, the helmet-for-hire phenomenon is alive and driving in ultra-professional, modern F1.

Just ask Japan's Ryo Hirakawa, who only last month achieved his "dream" , external when he got behind the wheel of a Haas at the Mexico City Grand Prix following Esteban Ocon's controversial departure from the team.

"I just need to taste this moment. I'm really happy," Hirakawa said after scoring a point - admittedly, following a few demotions for others. "Just enjoy this moment and see what we can do."

Within a week there was nothing the Toyota factory driver could do as Haas' 2027 driver Rafael Camara was drafted in for the American team early.

Hirakawa is a reserve driver for Haas as a result of the team's association with Toyota - the Japanese being in the right place at the right time.

title_en: Spy drama 'Slow Horses' to end with season 8, says actor Olivia Cook
summary_bn: The actor told The Times that she had always been keen to return to the show and that 'they were checking my availability over the years. And we stayed in touch. It was like I'd never left.'
summary_en: The actor told The Times that she had always been keen to return to the show and that 'they were checking my availability over the years. And we stayed in touch. It was like I'd never left.'
body_bn:
দ্য বিজনেস স্ট্যান্ডার্ড-এর প্রতিবেদন অনুযায়ী — Spy drama 'Slow Horses' to end with season 8, says actor Olivia Cook। The actor told The Times that she had always been keen to return to the show and that 'they were checking my availability over the years. And we stayed in touch. It was like I'd never left.'

Los Angeles – Popular spy series "Slow Horses", which revolves around a group of disgraced MI5 agents navigating the world of espionage under their notorious boss Jackson Lamb, will end after season 8, actor Olivia Cooke has said.

Cooke played Sid Baker in the first season of the drama, a character who is seemingly killed off at the end but returns to Slough House in the sixth season, Variety reported, quoting her interview with The Times.

"I am shooting the last season! Never say never! But I think that's what we've been told and it definitely feels like we are ending. We're all melancholy, distracted.

"Yesterday, I got in the make-up chair and cried. The show's been a shining light and I've told my partner I need two weeks to get over it. I'm going to be depressed," Cooke said.

However, her role in "House of the Dragon" made it difficult for her to return to "Slow Horses" earlier.

"There was something in my contract for 'House of the Dragon' which said I was not allowed to do a long-running series for an opposing streamer, so we had to smooth that out," she said, adding that lawyers got involved. "I sent texts saying, 'Help!'"

title_bn: Jay Shah reappointed ICC chairman for second successive term
title_en: Jay Shah reappointed ICC chairman for second successive term
summary_bn: Serving as chair of the ICC is both a privilege and a responsibility, said Jay shah.
summary_en: Serving as chair of the ICC is both a privilege and a responsibility, said Jay shah.
body_bn:
দ্য বিজনেস স্ট্যান্ডার্ড-এর প্রতিবেদন অনুযায়ী — Jay Shah reappointed ICC chairman for second successive term। Serving as chair of the ICC is both a privilege and a responsibility, said Jay shah.

India's Jay Shah has been appointed the chairman of the International Cricket Council (ICC) board for a second successive term following a proposal by the ICC directors at the global governing body's board meetings in Bali, Indonesia.

"The decision reflects the board's confidence in Shah's leadership and provides continuity at a defining moment for the sport, with global expansion, growth in fandom and commercial development central to its strategic roadmap," the ICC said in a statement today (16 November).

Shah said, "I am deeply honoured by the confidence the ICC Board has placed in me and sincerely grateful to every Director for their continued trust and support.

"Serving as chair of the ICC is both a privilege and a responsibility, and I remain committed to working with our members to advance the interests of cricket across the world."

He went on to say, "Cricket's greatest strength lies in its ability to bring people together. With the support of the Board and our members, our focus will be on turning ambition into action and ensuring that the progress we make leaves a lasting legacy for generations to come."

England ended world champions Spain's record unbeaten run with a 3-2 win in Madrid to top their Nations League group, but Italy's hopes of joining them in next year's quarter-finals were dashed as they lost 4-1 in Belgium yesterday (15 November).

Substitute Nico Williams then made it 3-2, but England survived a late siege to secure a statement victory.

Spain could have few complaints as they were second best for much of the game, although they also progress to the quarter-finals as runners-up.

Landmarks in Miami are lighting up with its alter ego "Vice City" in the run-up to the much-anticipated launch of the latest instalment of the Grand Theft Auto (GTA) video game.

Millions of fans have been waiting for more than a decade for GTA VI, and the city that inspired the series is awash with ads for it ahead of the 19 November release.

Miami-Dade County officials signed a $3.9 million deal with GTA developer Rockstar Games to place advertisements in iconic locations like the stadium of the Miami Heat basketball franchise and the city's airport.

The neon-pink inscription of Vice City can also be seen on storage containers on Miami Beach, on giant murals on downtown boulevards, boxing rings and even on coffee cups.

That's feeding into feverish anticipation from local fans of the video game.

title_bn: Railway plans to convert Tk358-cr unused luggage vans into passenger coaches
title_en: Railway plans to convert Tk358-cr unused luggage vans into passenger coaches
summary_bn: The latest proposal is to modify the vans into coaches modelled on metro trains, with more standing space and limited seating, primarily to accommodate passengers travelling on standing tickets. No final decision has been made yet
summary_en: The latest proposal is to modify the vans into coaches modelled on metro trains, with more standing space and limited seating, primarily to accommodate passengers travelling on standing tickets. No final decision has been made yet
body_bn:
দ্য বিজনেস স্ট্যান্ডার্ড-এর প্রতিবেদন অনুযায়ী — Railway plans to convert Tk358-cr unused luggage vans into passenger coaches। The latest proposal is to modify the vans into coaches modelled on metro trains, with more standing space and limited seating, primarily to accommodate passengers travelling on standing tickets. No final decision has been made yet

Bangladesh Railway is considering converting 125 luggage vans, bought for Tk358 crore with foreign loans to boost freight revenue, into passenger coaches after failing to put them to effective use for nearly three years.

Imported from China in 2023 without adequate assessment of their operational feasibility, the vans have largely remained idle despite several initiatives to use them for transporting goods, including attaching them to intercity trains and leasing them to private operators. Only around 5% are currently in use.

Fakir Md Mohiuddin, additional director general (rolling stock) of Bangladesh Railway, told The Business Standard that the railway minister had instructed officials to examine whether the vans could be used to carry passengers.

"We have formed two committees, involving the general managers of the railway's two zones. Once we receive their reports and recommendations on whether the luggage vans should be used for freight or converted into passenger coaches, we will decide on the next steps," he said.

Transport expert Professor Dr Md Shamsul Haque of Bangladesh University of Engineering and Technology (Buet) told TBS last year that the railway had failed to properly assess the usefulness of the vans before purchasing them. "Railway officials make big claims that buying luggage vans and wagons will increase freight transport. But their effectiveness was not properly assessed before the purchase. Sometimes such procurement is made to benefit suppliers. Nobody takes responsibility. The government should investigate and ensure accountability," the professor said.

According to railway records, on 23 October 2014, then prime minister Sheikh Hasina instructed the railway authorities to attach luggage vans to passenger trains during a visit to the Railways Ministry. Of the 50 vans then in the railway fleet, 32 were out of service.

দ্য বিজনেস স্ট্যান্ডার্ড-এর প্রতিবেদন অনুযায়ী — Hridoy, Litton lift Bangladesh to record 327/6 after Rabada five-for। He then had Mominul Haque caught behind and bowled captain Najmul Hossain Shanto with an inswinging full delivery, leaving Bangladesh on 22 for three in the ninth over.

Towhid Hridoy struck 137 and shared a record 206-run stand with Litton Das to lift Bangladesh to 327 for six on the opening day of the first Test against South Africa in Johannesburg today (15 November).

It is Bangladesh's highest total against South Africa in Tests. Litton will resume on 92 on the second day.

Hridoy was lbw to Marco Jansen off the last ball of the day, ending a sixth-wicket stand that is now Bangladesh's highest against South Africa, home or away.

The previous best was 138, by Jaker Ali and Mehidy Hasan Miraz for the seventh wicket in Mirpur in 2024.

The pair came together after Kagiso Rabada had taken all five Bangladesh wickets to fall, reducing them to 121 for five.

Rabada struck with the first ball of the match, when debutant Mahfizul Islam was caught by Jansen at gully.

দ্য বিজনেস স্ট্যান্ডার্ড-এর প্রতিবেদন অনুযায়ী — Filmmaker Sohel Rahman turns personal loss into a debut film about cancer। Filmmaker Sohel Rahman has completed his first feature film, 'Hawar Gaari' (The Wind Car). It tells the story of working-class life in Dhaka and the unequal fight against cancer, with love, hope and resilience at its heart. The film was produced under the banner of Vila Do Cinema. Its final cut was finished in November after four months o

Chitralekha Guha, Fazlul Haque, Ayman Shimla, Yashfa Tasnia Mallick, Omar Faruque, Tridha Paul Maan and Shobdo play the leading roles.

The story comes from a tragedy in the director's own life. A month after their wedding, his wife, Dr Shamrina Tanha, was diagnosed with cancer. For nearly a year, Sohel took her from hospital to hospital across Dhaka in search of treatment. She died in March this year.

Yet the film reaches beyond one family's grief. Its characters face illness, poverty and uncertainty, but they keep fighting to live with dignity. Moving between tears and laughter, it explores how love and hope survive in the hardest circumstances.

'Hawar Gaari' was made quickly and on a modest budget. The script, locations, cast and crew were finalised in April and May, and shooting wrapped in Dhaka in June. Post-production began in July.

Most of the crew are Sohel's own students. Several established and emerging Bangladeshi artists joined the project willingly, and friends and well-wishers also lent their support.

title_bn: Cape Verde votes in presidential election that could make history with first female president
title_en: Cape Verde votes in presidential election that could make history with first female president
summary_bn: With a population of around 500,000, Cape Verde is known for its competitive elections and peaceful transfers of power, a political tradition that remains uncommon in parts of West Africa.
summary_en: With a population of around 500,000, Cape Verde is known for its competitive elections and peaceful transfers of power, a political tradition that remains uncommon in parts of West Africa.
body_bn:
দ্য বিজনেস স্ট্যান্ডার্ড-এর প্রতিবেদন অনুযায়ী — Cape Verde votes in presidential election that could make history with first female president। With a population of around 500,000, Cape Verde is known for its competitive elections and peaceful transfers of power, a political tradition that remains uncommon in parts of West Africa.

Cape Verdeans went to the polls on Sunday (15 November) in a presidential election that could make history by electing the country's first female head of state since gaining independence from Portugal in 1975.

Former Justice Minister Joana Rosa is contesting the election against incumbent President José Maria Neves, who is seeking a second five-year term. Six candidates are vying for the presidency. If none secures more than 50% of the vote, a run-off election will be held on 29 November.

Rosa is backed by the opposition Movement for Democracy (MpD), which governed the country for a decade before losing the parliamentary election in May. Although women have held senior positions in the Cabinet, the island nation has never had a female prime minister or president.

Under Cape Verde's parliamentary system, the prime minister exercises most executive powers and oversees government policy. The president, who is directly elected, largely performs a ceremonial role but has the authority to veto legislation.

Nearly 77,000 citizens living abroad are registered to vote, accounting for almost one-fifth of the country's total electorate.

Roselma Évora, a professor of political science and gender studies at the University of Cabo Verde, said limited economic opportunities were prompting many young people to move abroad in search of better prospects.

Former adviser Asif Mahmud Shojib Bhuyain has said he could resolve the country's law and order situation if given responsibility for the Home Ministry for two weeks.

"If you cannot do it, give me the Home Ministry for two weeks. I'll fix things," he wrote in a Facebook post published at 3:27pm today (15 November).

His remark came amid growing concerns over a series of criminal incidents across the country, including crude bomb attacks, arson attacks, theft, snatching and other offences.

The post also came amid heightened tension in Gopalganj, where activists of the banned Awami League and its affiliated organisations staged processions, broke police barricades and allegedly vandalised a supershop earlier in the day.

Hundreds of activists reportedly gathered at different locations in the district town, chanting slogans in support of Awami League President Sheikh Hasina. They also set tyres on fire at several locations, prompting increased security deployment across the town.

The demonstrations disrupted normal activities, with shops temporarily closing and residents expressing concern over the situation.

Police, Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB), Armed Police Battalion (APBn) and other law enforcement personnel were deployed to maintain order.

title_en: Banned AL activists vandalise police vehicle, July memorial during procession in Gopalganj
summary_bn: DC withdrawn, SP transferred; 6 BGB platoons deployed.

body_bn:
দ্য বিজনেস স্ট্যান্ডার্ড-এর প্রতিবেদন অনুযায়ী — Banned AL activists vandalise police vehicle, July memorial during procession in Gopalganj। DC withdrawn, SP transferred; 6 BGB platoons deployed.

Leaders and activists of the banned Awami League and its affiliated organisations in Gopalganj today (15 November) vandalised an armoured personnel carrier (APC), a police box, a July memorial, university signage, and other public and private establishments while staging demonstrations in Gopalganj town.

The demonstrations and vandalism continued from 11am to 1:45pm, with hundreds of activists taking to the streets, chanting slogans in support of ousted prime minister Sheikh Hasina and her party.

After evening, miscreants set ablaze a branch office of Grameen Bank in Ulpur area of Tungipara upazila, said Ayub Ali, officer-in-charge of Tungipara Police Station.

Besides, the police station's sub-inspector Moslem, who filed a case over the vandalism of a police vehicle on 10 November, was hacked by miscreants equipped with sharp weapons, the OC said, adding that the injured officer was hospitalised.

Gopalganj DC and SP transferred in latest administrative reshuffle DC withdrawn, SP transferred Amid protests and vandalism, district Deputy Commissioner (DC) Md Arif-uz-Zaman has been withdrawn, while Superintendent of Police (SP) Md Habibullah has been transferred to Feni.

Habiganj DC GM Sarfaraz has been made the new DC of Gopalganj while Arif has been attached to the public administration ministry. Feni SP Pratyush Kumar Majumder has been transferred to Gopalganj.

Four more senior police officials were transferred at the same time.

title_en: RMG unrest: 50 factories remain closed in Savar-Ashulia, 13 shut indefinitely in Gazipur
summary_bn: A total of 48 platoons of law enforcement personnel have been deployed across industrial areas in Dhaka, Gazipur and Narayanganj to maintain law and order and protect factories.
summary_en: A total of 48 platoons of law enforcement personnel have been deployed across industrial areas in Dhaka, Gazipur and Narayanganj to maintain law and order and protect factories.
body_bn:
দ্য বিজনেস স্ট্যান্ডার্ড-এর প্রতিবেদন অনুযায়ী — RMG unrest: 50 factories remain closed in Savar-Ashulia, 13 shut indefinitely in Gazipur। A total of 48 platoons of law enforcement personnel have been deployed across industrial areas in Dhaka, Gazipur and Narayanganj to maintain law and order and protect factories.

Authorities have shut 13 garment factories in Gazipur indefinitely amid ongoing labour unrest, while five others have declared a one-day general holiday today (15 November).

Meanwhile, the Savar-Ashulia industrial belt remained largely calm today, but more than 50 factories in the area remains closed for various reasons.

The Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) has deployed 35 platoons across the three areas, while five platoons of Ansar and eight platoons of the Special Response Battalion (SRB) have been deployed in Gazipur. The forces in Gazipur are being led by 25 executive magistrates.

According to a BGB press release issued today (15 November), 18 BGB platoons are performing security duties in Savar and Ashulia, 10 in different industrial areas of Gazipur and seven in Narayanganj.

According to industrial police and local sources, workers have been staging protests and work stoppages in different parts of Gazipur over the past few days, demanding, among other things, a minimum wage of Tk30,000.

This morning, workers gathered in front of a factory in the Mouchak area of Kaliakair. They left the area about half an hour after law enforcement personnel arrived. Isolated incidents of unrest were also reported in the Konabari and Jarun areas of Gazipur city.

title_bn: After RMG, could the economy send more Bangladeshis back to the streets?
title_en: After RMG, could the economy send more Bangladeshis back to the streets?
summary_bn: Inflation is eroding purchasing power, investment remains weak and employment opportunities are scarce. Unless the government addresses these pressures, economic frustration could spill back onto the streets
summary_en: Inflation is eroding purchasing power, investment remains weak and employment opportunities are scarce. Unless the government addresses these pressures, economic frustration could spill back onto the streets
body_bn:
দ্য বিজনেস স্ট্যান্ডার্ড-এর প্রতিবেদন অনুযায়ী — After RMG, could the economy send more Bangladeshis back to the streets?। Inflation is eroding purchasing power, investment remains weak and employment opportunities are scarce. Unless the government addresses these pressures, economic frustration could spill back onto the streets

Over several days in early November, garment workers blocked roads across Gazipur, Savar, Ashulia and Narayanganj. Factories were vandalised. Vehicles were torched. Police used force. The Border Guard Bangladesh was deployed. At one point, production was suspended at 529 factories, affecting nearly 987,000 workers. The movement escalated unnaturally fast, and the tension has yet to ease. The risk is not confined to the ready-made garment (RMG) sector. It now looms over other sectors as well, as the cost of living keeps rising and families feel the pinch of inflation more sharply than before.

And it has strong political ramifications. Bangladesh emerged from the July Uprising with a changed political order, and the two successive administrations inherited a broken economy left by the previous Awami regime. The banking crisis remained. Investment remained weak. Energy shortages continued to constrain production.

Inflation kept eating into real wages. The formal job market remained unable to absorb the country's young people. And now the question arises whether all of these factors could trigger an outburst on the streets, as global examples have shown in recent months.

One of the key factors influencing the July Uprising was the economy. There was hope that once the corrupt, autocratic regime was removed, the economy would see better days. But that has not quite been the case.

Point-to-point inflation stood at 8.34% in September, rising from 8.26% in August. Inflation has remained above 8% for years, while wage growth has repeatedly failed to keep pace.

The outlook is worse. The World Bank projects growth of only 3.4% in both FY2025–26 and FY2026–27, citing weaker investment, slowing exports, energy constraints and financial-sector vulnerabilities. The IMF has cut its FY2026–27 growth projection to 3.2% while forecasting average inflation of 10.9%.

That combination of weak growth, high inflation and poor employment creation is the substance of stagflation, even if policymakers prefer less alarming vocabulary.

title_bn: Garment factory owner arrested within 24 hours over rape of 15-year-old
title_en: Garment factory owner arrested within 24 hours over rape of 15-year-old
summary_bn: The 60-year-old accused was arrested in Dhaka's Islampur in connection with the alleged rape in Munshiganj's Sirajdikhan.
summary_en: The 60-year-old accused was arrested in Dhaka's Islampur in connection with the alleged rape in Munshiganj's Sirajdikhan.
body_bn:
দ্য বিজনেস স্ট্যান্ডার্ড-এর প্রতিবেদন অনুযায়ী — Garment factory owner arrested within 24 hours over rape of 15-year-old। The 60-year-old accused was arrested in Dhaka's Islampur in connection with the alleged rape in Munshiganj's Sirajdikhan.

Police have arrested a garment factory owner within 24 hours of a case being filed over the rape of a 15-year-old girl in Munshiganj's Sirajdikhan upazila.

The accused, Anwar Majhi, 60, was arrested from Dhaka's Islampur area around 3:30am today (15 November) following an overnight operation, police said.

According to the police and the case statement, the incident took place around 2:30pm on 12 November at Anwar's private office at Indian Textile, a garment factory in the Kathaltali area of Jainshar union in Sirajdikhan.

The victim's mother alleged that Anwar locked the office door and raped her daughter before confining her inside the room.

The girl's mother, Halima Khatun, 49, had been working at the factory for nearly two months. According to the case statement, the girl was assigned to assist with office work in the owner's private office after her mother became acquainted with him.

The complaint further stated that family members went to the factory and rescued the girl after learning that she had been confined there.

Halima filed a written complaint with Sirajdikhan Police Station on 13 November. Police subsequently registered a case and launched an operation to arrest the accused

title_bn: Invest Bangladesh opens first overseas representative office in China
title_en: Invest Bangladesh opens first overseas representative office in China
summary_bn: Building on operational experience gained from the China office, the agency plans to expand its presence in other priority investment markets in phases.
summary_en: Building on operational experience gained from the China office, the agency plans to expand its presence in other priority investment markets in phases.
body_bn:
দ্য বিজনেস স্ট্যান্ডার্ড-এর প্রতিবেদন অনুযায়ী — Invest Bangladesh opens first overseas representative office in China। Building on operational experience gained from the China office, the agency plans to expand its presence in other priority investment markets in phases.

Invest Bangladesh today (15 November) launched its first overseas representative office in Guangzhou, China, as part of its strategic efforts to strengthen its presence in key source markets for foreign direct investment (FDI).

The Guangzhou office will serve as a dedicated local point of contact for prospective Chinese investors, providing investment information, regulatory guidance and direct assistance in connecting with relevant authorities in Bangladesh.

The initiative fulfils a commitment announced in March this year under Invest Bangladesh's 180-day investment action plan.

"Our aim is to engage directly with prospective investors and facilitate investment projects from an early stage," said Nahian Rahman Rochi, Head of Investment Development at Invest Bangladesh.

"We chose Guangzhou for its strong industrial base and extensive manufacturing network. We have brought in experienced Chinese professionals who know both markets and can make it easier for investors to move from initial interest to actual investment," he said.

The Guangzhou office is led by May Zhou, Chief Representative and Business Development Manager, alongside Yang Wenchuang, Representative and Business Development Analyst.

title_bn: Chattogram Wasa plans floating intakes to maintain water supply during dry season
title_en: Chattogram Wasa plans floating intakes to maintain water supply during dry season
summary_bn: The technology, a first in Bangladesh, will be installed in phases
summary_en: The technology, a first in Bangladesh, will be installed in phases
body_bn:
দ্য বিজনেস স্ট্যান্ডার্ড-এর প্রতিবেদন অনুযায়ী — Chattogram Wasa plans floating intakes to maintain water supply during dry season। The technology, a first in Bangladesh, will be installed in phases

Chattogram Water Supply and Sewerage Authority (Wasa) plans to install floating intakes at its water treatment plants to maintain normal water supply in the port city during the dry season.

Every year, from January to March or April, reduced water flow in the Karnaphuli River and increased salinity in the Halda River reduce Wasa's daily supply of drinking water by 80 to 100 million litres.

The authority has taken the initiative to introduce the new technology to address the situation.

Chattogram Wasa Managing Director Engineer Selim Md Jane Alam said although floating intake technology is used in various countries, Chattogram Wasa is taking the initiative to introduce it for the first time in Bangladesh.

"The plan will be implemented in phases," he said.

He explained that floating intakes automatically adjust their position as water levels rise or fall, allowing pumps to remain afloat and continue drawing water regardless of changes in river water levels.

This reduces the risk of pumps being submerged or running dry. The system also eliminates the need to reposition pumps or adjust pipe lengths as water depth changes.

BNP acting secretary general Ruhul Kabir Rizvi has alleged that the Awami League is now engaged in covert acts of sabotage across the country, including bombing, crude bomb explosions, arson attacks on vehicles and instigating unrest in the garment industry.

"Somewhere bombs are being hurled, somewhere crude bombs are being exploded, and vehicles are being set on fire. Various forms of disorder are also being created in the garment industry," he said while speaking to journalists after paying tribute at the mausoleums of late president Ziaur Rahman and former prime minister Khaleda Zia with leaders and activists of the newly formed Dhaka South BNP committee today (15 November).

"Railway authorities detected the matter quickly and took necessary measures, saving many lives," he said.

Rizvi alleged that supporters of ousted prime minister Sheikh Hasina are conspiring to create unrest across the country, both from within and outside Bangladesh, targeting roads, highways, railways and waterways.

He also accused them of creating unrest in garment factories they own.

He said the conspiracies will fail, as acts of sabotage are being detected and those involved arrested.

title_bn: Give Voyager 1 a flash: Nasa calls for a global light show on 17 November
title_en: Give Voyager 1 a flash: Nasa calls for a global light show on 17 November
summary_bn: The event, titled “Shine Bright for Voyager's Light-Day”, will take place after sunset, with participants encouraged to shine lights towards the night sky to mark the milestone, which comes nearly 50 years after the spacecraft was launched
summary_en: The event, titled “Shine Bright for Voyager's Light-Day”, will take place after sunset, with participants encouraged to shine lights towards the night sky to mark the milestone, which comes nearly 50 years after the spacecraft was launched
body_bn:
দ্য বিজনেস স্ট্যান্ডার্ড-এর প্রতিবেদন অনুযায়ী — Give Voyager 1 a flash: Nasa calls for a global light show on 17 November। The event, titled “Shine Bright for Voyager's Light-Day”, will take place after sunset, with participants encouraged to shine lights towards the night sky to mark the milestone, which comes nearly 50 years after the spacecraft was launched

Nasa is inviting people worldwide to take part in a public engagement event on Tuesday, 17 November 2026, to mark Voyager 1 becoming the first human-made object to reach a distance of one light-day from Earth.

The event, titled "Shine Bright for Voyager's Light-Day", will take place after sunset, with participants encouraged to shine lights towards the night sky to mark the milestone, which comes nearly 50 years after the spacecraft was launched.

A light-day is a measure of distance, referring to how far light travels in one day.

Participants can use Nasa's automated flashing tool, available at go.nasa.gov/vgr, on a smartphone or tablet. The tool will automatically flash Voyager 1's call sign towards the sky.

Alternatively, people can use a torch, glow stick, solar lantern, bicycle light or mobile phone light to manually signal the letters V-G-R in Morse code.

The sequence consists of three short flashes followed by a long flash for the letter V, two long flashes followed by a short flash for G, and a short flash, a long flash and another short flash for R.

Short flashes, or dots, should last less than one second, while long flashes, or dashes, should last about one second. Participants should pause for at least a second between letters and repeat the sequence for about one minute.

title_bn: Gold-like objects worth Tk1.80cr seized from Dubai-returnee at Dhaka airport
title_en: Gold-like objects worth Tk1.80cr seized from Dubai-returnee at Dhaka airport
summary_bn: Acting on a tip-off, customs officials subjected him to an X-ray examination, which detected objects concealed in his rectum.
summary_en: Acting on a tip-off, customs officials subjected him to an X-ray examination, which detected objects concealed in his rectum.
body_bn:
দ্য বিজনেস স্ট্যান্ডার্ড-এর প্রতিবেদন অনুযায়ী — Gold-like objects worth Tk1.80cr seized from Dubai-returnee at Dhaka airport। Acting on a tip-off, customs officials subjected him to an X-ray examination, which detected objects concealed in his rectum.

Customs officials have seized nearly one kilogram of gold-like substances, including four egg-shaped objects concealed in a passenger's rectum and paste smeared into his underwear, at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport today (15 November).

The estimated value of the seized substances is around Tk1.80 crore, according to a preliminary assessment by the Customs Intelligence and Investigation Directorate (CIID).

The passenger, Hasan Mia, from Banshkhali upazila of Chattogram, arrived in Dhaka from Dubai on a US-Bangla Airlines flight, BS-342, at 4:25am today.

They also found an estimated 100 grams of gold-like paste smeared into the fabric of his underwear, bringing the total weight of the recovered substances to around one kilogram.

The actual gold content and purity will be determined through testing and refining.

CIID suspects that an organised transnational smuggling syndicate may be involved and plans to coordinate with other domestic intelligence agencies to identify those behind the incident.

title_bn: German embassy to launch digital student visa application system for Bangladeshis in January
title_en: German embassy to launch digital student visa application system for Bangladeshis in January
summary_bn: The embassy's external service provider, VFS, will conduct a preliminary review of the submitted documents.
summary_en: The embassy's external service provider, VFS, will conduct a preliminary review of the submitted documents.
body_bn:
দ্য বিজনেস স্ট্যান্ডার্ড-এর প্রতিবেদন অনুযায়ী — German embassy to launch digital student visa application system for Bangladeshis in January। The embassy's external service provider, VFS, will conduct a preliminary review of the submitted documents.

The German Embassy in Dhaka will introduce a digital application system for student visas from 1 January, aiming to simplify the application process and reduce appointment waiting times for Bangladeshi students seeking to pursue bachelor's and master's degrees in Germany.

The Embassy of the Federal Republic of Germany in Dhaka announced the initiative in a press release today (15 November), saying the new system will operate through the Consular Services Portal, also known as the Auslandsportal.

Under the new system, applicants will be able to complete visa application forms and upload required documents online before attending an in-person appointment.

Applicants will also be able to track updates on their applications through the digital portal and submit joint applications with family members, where applicable.

According to the embassy, the new process is designed to make visa applications more transparent and predictable while improving document verification and overall processing efficiency.

The embassy said the existing appointment waiting list under the previous system will be discontinued by the end of 2026.

It represents nearly 694 million people, or 8.4% of the global population

The Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) is holding its final annual summit from 15 to 17 November in Manila, the Philippines, with regional leaders set to discuss energy security, trade tensions, territorial disputes and ongoing conflicts.

ASEAN aims to establish a single market, although it cannot impose decisions on its members.

Alongside leaders and representatives from its 11 member countries, the summit is expected to bring together several prominent international figures.

US President Donald Trump is scheduled to hold a special summit with ASEAN on 17 November, amid ongoing trade tensions with China. He is also due to hold a bilateral meeting with Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr.

Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva is attending in what the source describes as "the first by a sitting Brazilian president to the Philippines". His visit is expected to focus on trade, defence and bilateral cooperation.

Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney is set to deliver a speech at the summit, while Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi is attending as a "key trading partner to member states".

A late freedom fighter and local political leader from Shibchar in Madaripur has been named as an accused in a case over a road blockade, vandalism and crude bomb explosions at the Padma Bridge south toll plaza, seven and a half months after his death.

A resident of Dhalikandi in Kutubpur union of Shibchar upazila, Shamchu Dhali was the acting president of the union unit of the activity-banned Awami League.

At around 1:30am on 10 November, leaders and activists of the Awami League, whose activities are banned, and its affiliated organisations blocked the road in front of the Padma Bridge south toll plaza in Shariatpur's Jajira upazila.

During the blockade, several vehicles were vandalised and multiple crude bombs were exploded, suspending toll collection for around an hour and leaving vehicles stranded at both ends of the bridge.

On 12 November, Sub-Inspector Akram Hossain of Padma Bridge South Police Station filed a case under the Anti-Terrorism Act, naming 251 people and accusing another 600 to 700 unidentified individuals.

Shamchu Dhali's family expressed shock and anger over his inclusion in the case.

title_bn: Bangladesh hopes to finalise new IMF loan framework by January-February
title_en: Bangladesh hopes to finalise new IMF loan framework by January-February
summary_bn: The initiative signals a move away from simply continuing the previous loan programme towards developing a new financing framework that reflects the country's current economic conditions and the priorities of the elected government.
summary_en: The initiative signals a move away from simply continuing the previous loan programme towards developing a new financing framework that reflects the country's current economic conditions and the priorities of the elected government.
body_bn:
দ্য বিজনেস স্ট্যান্ডার্ড-এর প্রতিবেদন অনুযায়ী — Bangladesh hopes to finalise new IMF loan framework by January-February। The initiative signals a move away from simply continuing the previous loan programme towards developing a new financing framework that reflects the country's current economic conditions and the priorities of the elected government.

The government hopes to reach a final decision on a new loan programme and financing framework with the International Monetary Fund (IMF) by January-February next year, as discussions and technical-level work between the two sides continue.

The final decision will follow negotiations over the terms of the proposed programme, the amount of financing and the nature of the required reforms, Finance and Planning Minister Amir Khosru Mahmud Chowdhury disclosed the timeline while speaking to journalists after inaugurating Bangladesh's first international debt conference at Ocean Paradise Hotel in Cox's Bazar today (15 November).

The discussions with the IMF have covered exchange rate management, reforms in the banking sector, reducing subsidies on electricity and fertiliser, and increasing revenue collection.

The minister said working groups from both sides were continuing discussions on the new financing framework, with the aim of reaching a final settlement by January-February.

"We have not fallen behind because of IMF conditions. The loan programme was taken up with the IMF during the fascist regime. There are many issues in it that an elected government cannot implement. Reforms in many areas require continuity and a specific sequence. That takes time," Khosru said.

"If I try to carry out these reforms overnight, I will have to make certain decisions whose consequences will be borne by the people. This will harm the economy and businesses as well. An unelected government has no accountability to the people. It wanted to proceed in whatever way it saw fit," he added.

title_bn: Rainfall set to remain below normal in Nov after 68% deficit in Oct
title_en: Rainfall set to remain below normal in Nov after 68% deficit in Oct
summary_bn: A comparison of the two months shows that rainfall remained substantially below normal in October, while November is also expected to see limited precipitation, signalling a continuation of predominantly dry weather.
summary_en: A comparison of the two months shows that rainfall remained substantially below normal in October, while November is also expected to see limited precipitation, signalling a continuation of predominantly dry weather.
body_bn:
দ্য বিজনেস স্ট্যান্ডার্ড-এর প্রতিবেদন অনুযায়ী — Rainfall set to remain below normal in Nov after 68% deficit in Oct। A comparison of the two months shows that rainfall remained substantially below normal in October, while November is also expected to see limited precipitation, signalling a continuation of predominantly dry weather.

Bangladesh is likely to experience another relatively dry month in November, following a significant rainfall deficit in October, although the possibility of one to two cyclones developing over the Bay of Bengal remains, according to the Bangladesh Meteorological Department (BMD).

The country received an average of just 57mm of rainfall in October against the normal 179mm, registering a deficit of 68%.

The dry conditions are expected to persist in November, with rainfall forecast to remain below normal across all eight divisions.

According to the BMD's November long-range forecast, the country may receive 5- 40 mm of rainfall in different divisions, compared with their respective monthly averages of 6- 44 mm.

The number of rainy days is also expected to remain limited to two to four days across the divisions.

In October, Chattogram recorded the highest rainfall deficit at 80.6%, followed by Dhaka at 79.9%. Sylhet had the lowest deficit at 58.3%.

title_bn: How will the next UN secretary-general will be chosen?
title_en: How will the next UN secretary-general will be chosen?
summary_bn: The selection process involves secret ballots, informal voting rounds and geopolitical negotiations
summary_en: The selection process involves secret ballots, informal voting rounds and geopolitical negotiations
body_bn:
দ্য বিজনেস স্ট্যান্ডার্ড-এর প্রতিবেদন অনুযায়ী — How will the next UN secretary-general will be chosen?। The selection process involves secret ballots, informal voting rounds and geopolitical negotiations

The process to select the next United Nations secretary-general is entering a critical stage, with incumbent Antonio Guterres due to step down on 31 December 2026.

Eight candidates are competing for the position, but the outcome will depend largely on negotiations among the five permanent members of the UN Security Council (UNSC), which holds the authority to recommend a candidate to the General Assembly, says Al Jazeera.

Under Article 97 of the UN Charter, the Security Council selects a candidate and recommends that person to the 193-member UN General Assembly (UNGA) for formal approval.

The Security Council has 15 members: five permanent members and 10 elected non-permanent members. The permanent members, known as the P5, are China, France, Russia, the United Kingdom and the US.

A candidate needs at least nine votes in favour of their recommendation and must avoid a veto from any of the five permanent members.

The 10 elected non-permanent members currently include Bahrain, Colombia, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Denmark, Greece, Latvia, Liberia, Pakistan, Panama and Somalia.
